thinkBeforeYouCode.question: What is the Template Method pattern, and how does BaseSender use it?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: In BaseSender, the public send() method defines the invariant execution template: 1. Validate recipient -> 2. Format log -> 3. Call abstract deliver() -> 4. Record result. Subclasses only supply step 3, guaranteeing uniform logging and validation across all channels.

thinkBeforeYouCode.question: Why use an abstract class in addition to an interface?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: The interface defines the public API contract (send), while the abstract class provides reusable behavior (common validation and audit logging) that all concrete senders share, avoiding duplicate code.

thinkBeforeYouCode.question: How does this architecture support adding Slack or Discord notifications?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: You simply create a new class SlackSender extends BaseSender and implement deliver(). You can register it with NotificationDispatcher without changing a single line of dispatcher code.

# Multi-Channel Notification Service (Java OOP)

## Overview
A decoupled, enterprise alert dispatching engine in Java demonstrating abstraction, interface-driven routing, and the Template Method pattern across Email, SMS, and Push notification channels.

## Architecture Blueprint
```
                                +---------------------------------+
                                |       <<interface>>             |
                                |     NotificationSender          |
                                +---------------------------------+
                                | + send(to: String, msg: String) |
                                | + getChannelName(): String      |
                                +---------------------------------+
                                                 ^
                                                 |
                                +---------------------------------+
                                |       <<abstract class>>        |
                                |           BaseSender            |
                                +---------------------------------+
                                | - deliveryCount: int            |
                                +---------------------------------+
                                | + send(to: String, msg: String) | (Template Method)
                                | # deliver(to: Str, msg: Str): b | (Abstract)
                                +---------------------------------+
                                                 ^
                                                 |
          +--------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+
          |                                      |                                      |
+-----------------------+              +-----------------------+              +-----------------------+
|      EmailSender      |              |       SmsSender       |              |      PushSender       |
+-----------------------+              +-----------------------+              +-----------------------+
| # deliver(...): bool  |              | # deliver(...): bool  |              | # deliver(...): bool  |
| (Subject + Body)      |              | (160-char truncation) |              | (Push JSON Payload)   |
+-----------------------+              +-----------------------+              +-----------------------+
```

## Key Architectural Patterns
- **Template Method Pattern**: `BaseSender.send()` implements invariant audit and validation logic before calling subclass `deliver()`.
- **Decoupled Dispatcher**: `NotificationDispatcher` routes alerts polymorphically to registered channels.
- **Extensibility**: Adding new channels (e.g. Slack, Webhook) requires zero changes to core dispatcher code.

## How to Run
```bash
javac NotificationSender.java BaseSender.java EmailSender.java SmsSender.java PushSender.java NotificationDispatcher.java AlertApp.java
java AlertApp
```

## Sample Console Output
```text
=======================================================
           SYSTEM ALERT BROADCAST DISPATCH             
=======================================================
[EMAIL] -> devops-team@cloudcorp.com
  Subject: [CRITICAL ALERT] Database latency exceeded 500ms
  Body: Production replica node latency is critical. Immediate response required.
  Status: DELIVERED

[SMS] -> +15550198822
  Message: [CRITICAL ALERT] Production replica latency critical. Immed...
  Length: 68/160 chars | Status: DELIVERED

[PUSH] -> fcm-device-tok-84920492849284928492
  Payload: {"title":"CRITICAL ALERT","body":"Replica latency critical"}
  Status: DELIVERED
=======================================================
Broadcast Summary: 3/3 channels delivered successfully.
```

thinkBeforeYouCode.question: What is the Template Method pattern, and how does BaseSender use it?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: In BaseSender, the public send() method defines the invariant execution template: 1. Validate recipient -> 2. Format log -> 3. Call abstract deliver() -> 4. Record result. Subclasses only supply step 3, guaranteeing uniform logging and validation across all channels.

thinkBeforeYouCode.question: Why use an abstract class in addition to an interface?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: The interface defines the public API contract (send), while the abstract class provides reusable behavior (common validation and audit logging) that all concrete senders share, avoiding duplicate code.

thinkBeforeYouCode.question: How does this architecture support adding Slack or Discord notifications?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: You simply create a new class SlackSender extends BaseSender and implement deliver(). You can register it with NotificationDispatcher without changing a single line of dispatcher code.

hintSystem.level1Conceptual: In the abstract class, send() validates and logs, then delegates to deliver().
hintSystem.level2Implementation: Make send() final so subclasses cannot accidentally bypass the audit log.

hintSystem.level1Conceptual: Check length; if > 160, slice first 157 characters and add '...'.

normalCases: Email alert sent to devops@company.com -> Delivered with subject 'SYSTEM ALERT: Database latency elevated'
SMS sent to +15550192831 (45 chars) -> Delivered intact without truncation
Push notification sent to 32-char token -> Formatted and dispatched to mobile notification center
boundaryCases: SMS with exactly 160 characters -> Delivered intact with 0 characters truncated
SMS with 161 characters -> Safely truncated to 157 characters + '...'
invalidInputCases: Email recipient without '@' (e.g. 'alex_company') -> Validation fails, delivery aborted
Push notification with empty or null device token -> Rejected safely
edgeCases: Broadcasting a critical security alert across Email, SMS, and Push simultaneously with verified audit trails

debuggingGuide: Cannot instantiate the type BaseSender: Remember abstract classes cannot be directly instantiated with 'new BaseSender()'; you must instantiate concrete subclasses.
Subclass does not implement inherited abstract method: Ensure your subclasses provide an implementation of protected abstract boolean deliver().
StringIndexOutOfBoundsException in SMS truncation: Only call substring(0, 157) when message.length() > 160.
Overriding final template method: If send() is marked final in the base class, subclasses must override deliver() instead of send().

gitHubReady.readmeTemplate:
# Multi-Channel Notification Service (Java OOP)

## Overview
A decoupled, enterprise alert dispatching engine in Java demonstrating abstraction, interface-driven routing, and the Template Method pattern across Email, SMS, and Push notification channels.

## Architecture Blueprint
```
                                +---------------------------------+
                                |       <<interface>>             |
                                |     NotificationSender          |
                                +---------------------------------+
                                | + send(to: String, msg: String) |
                                | + getChannelName(): String      |
                                +---------------------------------+
                                                 ^
                                                 |
                                +---------------------------------+
                                |       <<abstract class>>        |
                                |           BaseSender            |
                                +---------------------------------+
                                | - deliveryCount: int            |
                                +---------------------------------+
                                | + send(to: String, msg: String) | (Template Method)
                                | # deliver(to: Str, msg: Str): b | (Abstract)
                                +---------------------------------+
                                                 ^
                                                 |
          +--------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+
          |                                      |                                      |
+-----------------------+              +-----------------------+              +-----------------------+
|      EmailSender      |              |       SmsSender       |              |      PushSender       |
+-----------------------+              +-----------------------+              +-----------------------+
| # deliver(...): bool  |              | # deliver(...): bool  |              | # deliver(...): bool  |
| (Subject + Body)      |              | (160-char truncation) |              | (Push JSON Payload)   |
+-----------------------+              +-----------------------+              +-----------------------+
```

## Key Architectural Patterns
- **Template Method Pattern**: `BaseSender.send()` implements invariant audit and validation logic before calling subclass `deliver()`.
- **Decoupled Dispatcher**: `NotificationDispatcher` routes alerts polymorphically to registered channels.
- **Extensibility**: Adding new channels (e.g. Slack, Webhook) requires zero changes to core dispatcher code.

## How to Run
```bash
javac NotificationSender.java BaseSender.java EmailSender.java SmsSender.java PushSender.java NotificationDispatcher.java AlertApp.java
java AlertApp
```

## Sample Console Output
```text
=======================================================
           SYSTEM ALERT BROADCAST DISPATCH             
=======================================================
[EMAIL] -> devops-team@cloudcorp.com
  Subject: [CRITICAL ALERT] Database latency exceeded 500ms
  Body: Production replica node latency is critical. Immediate response required.
  Status: DELIVERED

[SMS] -> +15550198822
  Message: [CRITICAL ALERT] Production replica latency critical. Immed...
  Length: 68/160 chars | Status: DELIVERED

[PUSH] -> fcm-device-tok-84920492849284928492
  Payload: {"title":"CRITICAL ALERT","body":"Replica latency critical"}
  Status: DELIVERED
=======================================================
Broadcast Summary: 3/3 channels delivered successfully.
```
